name: Piper PA-16 Clipper / PA-20 Pacer
summary: Tailwheel four-seat 'short-wing Piper' of 1949–54: the Pacer is the conventional-gear forerunner of the Tri-Pacer, with the same short rectangular wing and boxy fabric fuselage. The PA-16 Clipper is a shorter two-seat version.

wings: High wing braced by one strut per side
Short, rectangular constant-chord wing with rounded tips
engines: Single flat-four in a short cowl
fuselage: Fixed main gear with a tailwheel
tail: Tall, squared fin and rudder on a low horizontal tail

tellTales: Short rectangular high wing on a boxy fabric fuselage with a tailwheel
Squared, tall tail on a stubby, nose-high airplane
Strut-braced high wing with a deep, four-window cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Pacer sits on a tailwheel; the Tri-Pacer is the same airframe with a nosewheel.
The Pacer has a short, rectangular fabric wing and a boxy fuselage; the 170 has a longer wing with tapered outer panels and a rounded, metal fuselage.
The Pacer is a deeper four-seat cabin with a short, stubby wing; the Super Cub is a tandem two-seater with a longer, narrower wing.
The Pacer has a short wing and a squared tail; the Stinson 108 has a longer wing and a large, curved tail.
